- **Origin (1970s)**  
  • First slogans appeared on “flea‑market” t‑shirts sold in Chicago, blending pop culture phrases with simple graphics.  

- **Rise of Political & Political-Brooke (1970–1990)**  
  • Punk and activist groups used slogans to make quick, punchy statements (e.g., “Fuck the Police”).  
  • Mainstream brands began licensing famous quotes and pop‑culture catch‑phrases for mass‑market tees.  

- **Digital Printing Revolution (1990s‑2000s)**  
  • Point‑of‑sale and digital ink‑jet printing turned custom slogan shirts from niche hobby into widely available product.  
  • Rapid‑turnaround orders allowed consumers to have fresh, up‑to‑date references (TV shows, memes) almost instantly.  

- **Social‑Media Influenced Content (2010s)**  
  • Hashtag slogans (e.g., “#BlackLivesMatter”) turned shirts into amplifying tools for movements and personal branding.  
  • DIY platforms (e.g., Teespring, Redbubble) let creators monetize memes, shout‑outs, and self‑photographed humor.  

- **Sustainability & Personalization Challenge (2020s)**  
  • Growing demand for eco‑friendly, locally‑sourced fabrics counter‑balances mass‑print or “print‑on‑demand” practices.  
  • Incorporating QR codes or AR experiences turns static slogans into interactive storytelling, blending apparel with digital engagement.
